name: McCall
summary: A mountain town on a glacial lake halfway down Idaho — beaches and old-growth ponderosa in summer, a ski hill and a carnival of snow sculptures in winter, and the reason the length of this state no longer has to be driven in one day.

lodging.name: Shore Lodge, or a cabin on Payette Lake
lodging.blurb: A 1948 lodge right on the water at the north end of town.

foodMustTry.name: Idaho rainbow trout
foodMustTry.blurb: Out of the Payette lakes and rivers, and on every menu in town.

days.label: Day 519 — Payette Lake, then the Capital
days.summary: A morning on the lake and an afternoon down the Payette River.

item.title: Payette Lake & Ponderosa State Park
item.blurb: A peninsula of old-growth ponderosa reaching out into a glacial lake, with trails along the bluff and sandy coves at the end of them. The water is snowmelt-clear and startlingly cold — swim anyway.

drive.scenicNote: ID-55 down the Payette River canyon — two hours of whitewater on your right, with kayakers running the drops at Banks and the rafting put-ins one after another.

item.title: Freak Alley Gallery
item.blurb: The largest open-air mural gallery in the Northwest, filling a downtown alley and repainted every summer — a good, loose first hour in a new city.
